quizzes.title: Nature's Basics
quizzes.description: Warm-up questions on plants, planets, animals and the human body.

questions.q: What is H₂O more commonly known as?
questions.note: Each water molecule has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

questions.q: A spider has eight legs.
questions.note: Spiders are arachnids, not insects, which have six legs.

questions.q: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.note: Iron oxide, basically rust, in its dust gives Mars its colour.

questions.q: What is the largest planet in our Solar System?
questions.note: More than 1,300 Earths could fit inside Jupiter.

questions.q: How many bones are there in the adult human body?
questions.note: Babies are born with around 300 bones, many of which fuse as they grow.

questions.q: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.note: Au comes from aurum, the Latin word for gold.

questions.q: Sound travels faster than light.
questions.note: Light is far faster, which is why you see lightning before you hear thunder.

questions.q: Which of these is the hardest natural material?
questions.note: Diamond tops the Mohs hardness scale at 10.

questions.q: At sea level, water boils at how many degrees Celsius?
questions.note: That is 212 degrees Fahrenheit.

questions.q: Which vitamin does your skin make when it is in sunlight?
questions.note: Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium for strong bones.

quizzes.title: Pages & Paintings
quizzes.description: Famous novels, playwrights and masterpieces from the world of art and books.

questions.q: Who wrote the novel 'Don Quixote'?
questions.note: Published in two parts, in 1605 and 1615; it is often called the first modern novel.

questions.q: Who wrote the novel Pride and Prejudice?
questions.note: It was first published in 1813.

questions.q: The Odyssey is an ancient Greek epic poem attributed to Homer.
questions.note: It follows Odysseus on his long journey home after the Trojan War.

questions.q: Which museum is home to the Mona Lisa?
questions.note: The Louvre in Paris is the world's most visited art museum.

questions.q: Which author created the Belgian detective Hercule Poirot?
questions.note: Accept Christie; Poirot debuted in The Mysterious Affair at Styles.

questions.q: Who wrote the novel Nineteen Eighty-Four?
questions.note: It gave us the phrase Big Brother is watching you.

questions.q: The ceiling of the Sistine Chapel was painted by Raphael.
questions.note: It was Michelangelo, who painted it between 1508 and 1512.

questions.q: Which Shakespeare play contains the line "To be, or not to be"?
questions.note: Prince Hamlet speaks it in Act 3.

questions.q: Which Spanish artist co-founded Cubism and painted Guernica?
questions.note: Accept Picasso; he developed Cubism with Georges Braque.

questions.q: Who wrote The Old Man and the Sea?
questions.note: It won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction in 1953.

quizzes.title: Eureka Moments
quizzes.description: The minds and breakthroughs behind the inventions that changed the world.

questions.q: Who discovered penicillin in 1928?
questions.note: He noticed mould killing bacteria on a dish left out in his lab.

questions.q: Which scientist is famous for the equation E = mc²?
questions.note: It appeared in 1905, the year Einstein published four landmark papers.

questions.q: The Wright brothers made their first powered aeroplane flight in 1903.
questions.note: The first flight, near Kitty Hawk, lasted just 12 seconds.

questions.q: Which English scientist set out the three laws of motion?
questions.note: Accept Newton; the laws appeared in his Principia in 1687.

questions.q: Which scientist discovered the elements radium and polonium?
questions.note: She was the first person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences.

questions.q: Johannes Gutenberg is famous for developing which invention?
questions.note: His movable-type press in Mainz dates from around 1440.

questions.q: Alexander Graham Bell invented the radio.
questions.note: Bell is known for the telephone; Guglielmo Marconi pioneered radio.

questions.q: Who wrote On the Origin of Species, setting out evolution by natural selection?
questions.note: It was published in 1859.

questions.q: Which system of raised dots lets blind people read by touch?
questions.note: Louis Braille developed it in the 1820s, while he was still a teenager.

questions.q: Which instrument did Galileo turn to the night sky in 1609?
questions.note: With it he discovered four moons of Jupiter in 1610.

quizzes.title: Turning Points
quizzes.description: Empires, treaties and pioneers that shaped world history.

questions.q: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
questions.note: It fell on 9 November 1989.

questions.q: The Hundred Years' War lasted exactly 100 years.
questions.note: It ran from 1337 to 1453, which is 116 years.

questions.q: Which Wonder of the Ancient World stood in the city of Alexandria?
questions.note: The lighthouse stood on the island of Pharos, giving the word for lighthouse in several languages.

questions.q: Who was the first Roman emperor?
questions.note: Accept Octavian, his name before he became emperor in 27 BC.

questions.q: Which empire was ruled from Constantinople until the city fell in 1453?
questions.note: The Ottomans captured the city and later made it their capital.

questions.q: Which treaty, signed in 1919, formally ended the First World War with Germany?
questions.note: It was signed in the Hall of Mirrors at the Palace of Versailles.

questions.q: Magellan's expedition made the first voyage around the globe, but Magellan himself died on the way.
questions.note: He was killed in the Philippines in 1521; Elcano completed the voyage in 1522.

questions.q: Who was the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic Ocean?
questions.note: She made the flight in 1932, landing in Northern Ireland.

questions.q: Which queen ruled England from 1558 to 1603?
questions.note: Accept Elizabeth; her reign is known as the Elizabethan era.

questions.q: In which year was the Magna Carta sealed by King John?
questions.note: It was sealed at Runnymede, beside the River Thames.
